acceptance_criteria.criterion: MoviesListView.axaml.cs Loaded handler catches exceptions and sets HasLoadError/LoadErrorMessage on the VM.
A CancellationTokenSource is created in the view and cancelled in the Unloaded handler.
Both LoadAsync and LoadFilterSlotsAsync receive the cancellation token.
Full test suite passes with no regressions.

summary: Refactored MoviesListView.axaml.cs: replaced anonymous Loaded lambda with named OnLoaded / OnUnloaded event handlers.
Added private CancellationTokenSource? _cts field; created in OnLoaded, cancelled and disposed in OnUnloaded.
Both vm.LoadAsync(token) and vm.LoadFilterSlotsAsync(token) now receive the token from the CTS.
Loaded handler wraps both calls in try/catch: OperationCanceledException is silently swallowed; all other exceptions set vm.HasLoadError = true and vm.LoadErrorMessage = ex.Message.
Added using Avalonia.Interactivity for RoutedEventArgs (System.Threading is a global implicit using — no explicit import needed).
Build: 0 errors, 0 warnings. Test run: 500 passed, 0 failed, 6 skipped.

comments.note: LoadFilterSlotsAsync (MoviesListViewModel.cs ~L263) has no internal error handling — unlike LoadAsync which catches non-cancellation exceptions internally, any exception from LoadFilterSlotsAsync propagates to all its callers. The view's Loaded handler now guards this path, but other future callers would not be protected. Consider adding a try/catch inside LoadFilterSlotsAsync mirroring the pattern in LoadAsync.

In MoviesListView.axaml.cs OnLoaded: if Loaded fires more than once (e.g., control re-attached to visual tree), the previous _cts instance is overwritten without being cancelled or disposed first, potentially leaking the old CancellationTokenSource. A guard at the top of OnLoaded — cancel and dispose any existing _cts before creating a new one — would prevent this edge-case leak.

LoadFilterSlotsAsync (MoviesListViewModel.cs ~L263) lacks internal error handling — exceptions propagate to callers unguarded. The view's Loaded handler now protects this call path, but future callers would not be. Developer already flagged as debt.

summary: Code review PASS. MoviesListView.axaml.cs implementation is clean, correct, and well-structured. All four acceptance criteria are met. The refactor from anonymous lambda to named OnLoaded/OnUnloaded handlers improves discoverability. CTS lifecycle management follows the correct cancel → dispose → null pattern. async void is appropriately used as this is an event handler — the one valid C# use case. Exception handling correctly separates OperationCanceledException (silent swallow) from general exceptions (propagated to VM). Two low-priority edge-case concerns were identified and are recorded as comments; neither is blocking.

comments.note: CTS re-attach guard (OnLoaded): if the control is ever detached and re-added to the visual tree, OnLoaded fires a second time and the existing _cts is overwritten without a prior Cancel/Dispose. Adding `_cts?.Cancel(); _cts?.Dispose();` at the top of OnLoaded before creating a new CTS would close this theoretical resource leak. This changes behavior in the re-attach scenario (cancels the previous in-flight load) so it is outside Fix-Forward scope — left as a tracked improvement for the Developer.

LoadFilterSlotsAsync (MoviesListViewModel.cs ~L263) has no internal error handling. The view's Loaded handler now protects this call site, but any future caller would receive unguarded exceptions. Mirroring the try/catch pattern that LoadAsync uses internally would make LoadFilterSlotsAsync robust regardless of its call site. Carried forward from Developer pipeline.

The sequential await pattern (LoadAsync then LoadFilterSlotsAsync) is acceptable. If profiling ever reveals a startup latency concern, Task.WhenAll could parallelize them — but only if the two operations are proven independent. No action needed now.

No observations — code is clean and consistent. Named handlers, correct CTS lifecycle, well-separated exception paths, and clear inline comment on the OperationCanceledException catch. Solid implementation.
